title: Five years by hand, seven weeks with Claude: my voxel wilderness engine, and the trailer Claude directed for it
author: WhatHasKHANGotToSay
selftext:
Ochre is a Rust voxel (now wilderness!) engine I've been working on since 2021. The trailer is all running in-engine, cut to a theme I made with Suno.

Open source on GitHub: [https://github.com/rornic/ochre](https://github.com/rornic/ochre)

For five years it was a hobby project I picked up and dropped. By July it was still flat noise terrain under a cyan sky. In October I came back to it with Claude Code, and in seven weeks it's gone from about 4,000 lines to 59,000. Most of what you see in the trailer came from that stretch, built on the chunk streaming and meshing I wrote by hand years ago. Screenshot from July 2026 in comments so you can see how far it's come!

How Claude made the trailer:

* I gave it the song and rough timestamps for the builds and drops
* it scouted 24 generated worlds for waterfalls, canyons and viewpoints using my worldview skill, which lets it generate world PNGs, then wrote each shot as a camera path timed to the music
* it rendered every frame at 1080p60 headless on my RTX 2060 and cut it to the track
* it decided the waterfalls looked like staircases and fixed them in the engine before filming them

I still gave it a few rounds of notes (the cliff jump was five seconds late, the jungle haze was too green).

The creatures and music live in a game I'm building on top, which isn't public yet. Everything else is in the engine. If you want to see where it goes next, a star on GitHub helps a lot!

The "before" in July! Took me years of divided attention to get to this point.

comments.author: TheLastTuatara
comments.body: The engine is interesting, the trailer is not. Too long and repetitive.

replies.author: WhatHasKHANGotToSay
replies.body: Ha, that's fair. Claude did try and steer me to a shorter clip but I wanted to show the full music track.

replies.author: Shppo
replies.body:
you need to create an intro version of the song imo no longer than 60 seconds 

then recut the trailer with this

replies.author: WhatHasKHANGotToSay
replies.body: I will probably do exactly this, and figure out a better soundtrack.

replies.author: oSi7ENT
replies.body: The music track was pretty bad too fam. Sorry to tell you. It doesn’t fit the scope of what you did.

comments.author: oSi7ENT
comments.body: Trailer was 8 years long. Literally 20 seconds is enough

comments.author: oSi7ENT
comments.body:
I just read “Suno” and as someone who does music (producer for almost 27 years) it makes more sense as to why I hated it.

Suno isn’t bad, it’s just not a solution.

replies.author: WhatHasKHANGotToSay
replies.body:
Completely fair. I'm an engineer, so the technical stuff comes easy but the art / music not so much.

Any tips for good music results using gen AI, or better pull out my MIDI controller and just put in the time?

replies.author: oSi7ENT
replies.body: Nah you’re OK to use Suno, you just need to make sure that the music fits the idea. Hard to explain.

comments.author: Tiny_BlackHole
comments.body:
People are going to come at op with all sorts of negative stuff. Trailer too long. Wheres the game? Etc.

I dont care, this looks like a world . And sometimes thats enough. Nice work

replies.author: WhatHasKHANGotToSay
replies.body: Appreciate that! This is still a WIP so I'm prioritising "looks like a world" right now. Trailer is just a bonus :)

replies.author: Curious-Pen5547
replies.body: Oh boy, let me tell you about this game called minecraft then!

comments.author: kamilr641
comments.body: did Claude pick the worlds by inspecting the generated PNGs, or did the skill expose terrain data it could use to find waterfalls and viewpoints?

replies.author: WhatHasKHANGotToSay
replies.body: A bit of both. In addition to PNGs there's also a probe to figure out exact coordinates for features like canyons, waterfalls, biomes.

replies.author: kamilr641
replies.body: does the probe return every matching spot, or can it rank them by how good they'd be for a camera shot?

comments.author: WhatHasKHANGotToSay
comments.body: Pretty much, yes. A few weeks of effort spread out over years got me that far.

comments.author: kamilr641
comments.body: a useful next score might be how long a feature stays visible along a path. a dramatic spot that flashes past for half a second can still be a bad trailer shot

comments.author: zer0sumgames
comments.body: I enjoyed the trailer. World looks cool. Good job man.

comments.author: Professional_East281
comments.body: Im also making a voxel game. Your world generation is quite beautiful. My worry with making something this intricate is that it would be hard to fill with stuff thats interesting

replies.author: WhatHasKHANGotToSay
replies.body:
Yeah that’s a challenge I’m battling. 
I’ve found a landmark system that adds medium sized formations helps a lot to make the horizon more interesting than just flat land and mountains.

comments.author: ilganeli
comments.body: Congratulations bro! I remember the hate on the post the last time you posted it, I think your work is super cool and looks gorgeous.
